_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 4: Keck I / MOSFIRE (one preset per band: Y, J, H, K)
_meta.companion: data/round4/mosfire.md (same content as a Markdown section in the format of data/presets_research.md); same JSON structure as data/presets_sources_3.json. Key KTG02 points to the round-2 file. Entries may carry 'stage' (design vs as-built) and 'kind' (maximum vs typical). Top-level 'multiplex' holds the objects-per-exposure row.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values. alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (whitespace/glyph-normalised).
_meta.quote_normalisation: Quotes copied from pdftotext (layout and raw) / HTML text; Symbol-font private-use glyphs (mu, degree, double prime), degree/ordinal glyphs, primes, curly quotes, dashes and minus signs normalised; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells; pieces that differ only in punctuation/spacing are accepted.

mosfire.title: Keck I / MOSFIRE (cryogenic near-IR multi-object slit spectrograph: CSU slit mask, refractive collimator and camera, one 110.5 l/mm reflection grating in orders 6/5/4/3 for Y/J/H/K)
mosfire.recommended_preset: Four presets (Y, J, H, K) that differ only in order, grating stop and central wavelength. Common: D = 10.95 m, F = 13.66 (M12: "the Keck Cassegrain f/13.66 focal plane (nominal scale is 0.72516 mm/")"), slit 0.7" (the nominal width), nObj = 28 (MOSDEF average; 46 slits maximum), collimator = Lens (six-element refractive, f_col = 1813.0 mm), W = 1813.0/13.66 = 132.7 mm DERIVED (the design paper's "stipulated" 125.0 mm beam belongs to its effective f/14.50), f_cam = 250.0 mm, reflection grating G = 110.5 l/mm, blaze 21.93 deg = Littrow first-order blaze 67,597 A DERIVED (the published "6.35 um" is the blaze in the 40 deg geometry, not Littrow), fixed camera-collimator angle psi = 40 deg, HAWAII-2RG 2048 x 2048 x 18 um (17.984 um at 77 K) with Nx = 2048 along the dispersion. Per band (order; published grating stop; as-built lambda_c at the field centre; DERIVED alpha that puts lambda_c at the detector centre): Y (m = 6; 41.524 deg; 10373 A; 41.465 deg), J (m = 5; 41.524 deg; 12450 A; 41.469 deg), H (m = 4; 42.614 deg; 16321 A; 42.572 deg), K (m = 3; 42.614 deg; 21760 A; 42.570 deg). Validate against M12 Table 1 / Keck grating page: 1.0855 / 1.3028 / 1.6269 / 2.1691 A/px (model 1.0856 / 1.3027 / 1.6273 / 2.1698 DERIVED); K 19540-23970 A (model 19541-23972), H 14680-18040 A (model 14656-17980); the Y (9716-11250 A) and J (11530-13520 A) ranges are filter-limited and narrower than the detector span (model 9263-11481, 11118-13779); 0.7" slit image 2.92 px (YJ) / 2.87 px (HK) (model 2.915 / 2.867); 0.1798"/px; R(0.7") measured 3380 / 3310 / 3660 / 3620 (M12; Keck page 3388 / 3318 / 3660 / 3610) vs aberration-free model 3278 / 3279 / 3499 / 3498 (DERIVED). Alternative using the design angles exactly: lambda_c = 10400 / 12480 / 16350 / 21800 A at 41.524 / 42.614 deg (DERIVED from the M10 design statement "2.18", "1.635", "1.248", "1.04" um).

not_found: As-built collimator and camera focal lengths: only the design values 1813.0 mm and 250.0 mm (2007 DDR, 2010 paper). The as-built 7.25 reduction, 0.1798"/px and the four dispersions reproduce them (DERIVED), so they are used.
An as-built collimated beam diameter for the full 10.95 m primary: only the "stipulated" 125.0 mm at the effective f/14.50 (DERIVED 132.7 mm at f/13.66) and the ~138.4 mm Y-band open-hole pupil.
The pupil definition behind the effective f/14.50 (149.572 m / 14.50 = 10.315 m, DERIVED) -- not explained in M10 or MDDR.
As-built grating stop angles to better than 0.1 deg (M12 rounds to 42.6/41.5); the as-built lambda_c imply 42.57/41.47 deg (DERIVED).
As-built grating ruled area and blank size (only the DDR requirement ~266.7 x 187.96 mm elliptical).
The number of usable pixels along the dispersion: M12 gives an active area of 2040 x 2040 without stating why; the preset uses the full 2048.
Typical number of objects per mask from the instrument team: only survey values (MOSDEF average 28; KBSS 28-34) and the 46-slit maximum.

Kassis et al. 2016 (SPIE 9908, operational performance of the CSU) and McLean et al. 2008 (SPIE 7014, early design): not obtained or read (found only as SPIE listings); not needed for the optical parameters.
The MOSFIRE Requirements document v1.4 was downloaded and searched but contributed no value used here; not saved.
conflicts: Telescope focal ratio at the CSU: f/13.66 (M12, MPSR; = 149.572 m / 10.95 m) vs effective f/14.50 (M10, MDDR, with the 125.0 mm beam; = 149.572 m / 10.315 m DERIVED) vs nominal f/15 (S14, M10 "nominal f/15 focus", KTG02).
Collimated beam: 125.0 mm stipulated (M10, MDDR) vs 132.7 mm DERIVED for the full f/13.66 beam vs ~138.4 mm open-hole Y-band pupil image of the full serrated primary (MDDR).

Grating angles: 42.614/41.524 deg (M10; MDDR Secs. 3.1, 5.1.2.5) vs 41.525 deg for Y/J (MDDR Sec. 3.2.2 and Sec. 5.4.3.1.3.1 mechanism list) vs 42.614235/41.523692 deg (MDDR turret) vs 42.6/41.5 deg as built (M12, MPSR). Design lambda_c 2.18/1.635/1.248/1.04 um vs as-built 21760/16321/12450/10373 A (implies alpha 0.04-0.06 deg smaller, DERIVED).
Grating positions: "a single, fixed diffraction grating" (UCLA page, pre-DDR wording) vs two fixed angles (M10, M12, MPSR, MDDR).

Slit length: 7.01" (M12 text, MPSR) vs 7.0" (M12 abstract) vs 7.1" (M10, K15) vs 7.3" (MDDR Table 1, UCLA). Longer-slit increment: 7.5" (M12 abstract) vs 8" (MPSR) vs (8.0 N - 1.0)" (S14) vs 2 x 7.01 + 0.96 = 14.98" (M12) vs 15.0" (M10).
Number of slits: 46 (M10, M12, MPSR, S14, K15) vs ~45 (UCLA capabilities list).
Dispersion: 2.1691/1.6269 A/px (M12, KMG) vs 2.172/1.629 (S14) for K/H.
Coverage at the field centre: H 14680-18040, K 19540-23970 A (M12, KMG) vs 1.465-1.799 and 1.953-2.398 um (S14) vs design 1.48-1.81 and 1.97-2.42 um (M10).
Y-band range for slits at X = -1.5': 9716-11070 A (M12 Table 1) vs 9900-11250 A (KMG); both say 88%. H at +1.5': 14640-17440 (M12) vs 14640-17444 (KMG).
Resolution element in pixels for 0.7": geometric 2.92 (YJ) / 2.87 (HK) (M12) vs 2.82/2.88/2.74/2.78 (Y/J/H/K; KMG) vs ~2.7 (S14) vs 2.9 (M10, MDDR).
Overall wavelength range: 0.97-2.41 um (M12) vs 0.97-2.45 um (M10 abstract) vs 0.975-2.40 um (M10 Table 1, MDDR).
Pixel pitch: 18 um nominal (M10, MPSR, UCLA) vs 17.984 um at 77 K (M12).
notes: Sign convention for the app (as for DEIMOS): sin(alpha) + sin(beta) = m G lambda with alpha - beta = psi = 40 deg; at band centre beta = +1.5 deg (Y/J) and +2.6 deg (H/K), so the camera axis sits a few degrees from the grating normal -- M12: "the geometry, which has the grating normal only a few degrees from the optical axis" (source of the 0th-order ghosts).

Blaze convention: the explorer input lamB1 is the Littrow first-order blaze = 2 sin(21.93 deg)/110.5 = 67,597 A (DERIVED). The sources' "6.35 um" is the first-order blaze in MOSFIRE's 40 deg geometry (= Littrow x cos 20 deg, DERIVED); using 63,500 A as lamB1 would shift the blaze peaks ~6% to the blue.
H and K share one grating stop, Y and J the other, because m x lambda_c is nearly equal within each pair (DERIVED 65,280-65,284 A and 62,238-62,250 A).

Y and J coverage is set by the order-sorting filters (central-slit ranges equal the filter passbands); the 2048-px detector spans 2217 A (Y) and 2661 A (J) at the field centre (DERIVED), so the explorer's detector-limited coverage will exceed the published Y/J ranges. H and K are detector-limited at the field centre.

Slits at X = +/-1.5' (+/-65.2635 mm at the CSU) shift lambda_c by 6.216/7.460/9.157/12.209 A per mm (Y/J/H/K; M12, KMG): ~400-800 A at the field edge, which truncates the H and K spectra (82% retained).

Measured R (M12, KMG) exceeds the aberration-free geometric value (DERIVED 3278-3499) by 0.9-4.6%; KMG's R column equals lambda_c / (Resolution(pix) x A/px) with measured line FWHM 2.74-2.88 px, narrower than the 2.87-2.92 px geometric slit image.
KMR asks that MOSFIRE papers cite M12 and M10 ("McLean, I.S., Steidel, C.C. et al. 2012 ... SPIE Procs, 8446 17"; "... 2010 ... SPIE Procs, 7735 47").
Internal temperatures: optics at 120 K, detector at 77 K (M12 Sec. 2); the design was optimised with 120 K indices (M10).
